We can produce samples from the failure
distribution by sampling from the nominal
trajectory distribution and rejecting any samples
that are not failures!
What might be a problem with this method?
Hint: what theme seems to be coming up over and over again in this course?
It will be inefficient for systems with rare failure events!
One solution is to try to come up with a better proposal distribution.

So how do we create the chain?
Start with an initial sample τ.
At each iteration:
1
Sample τ′∼g(⋅∣τ)

(otherwise keep τ)
And so on…
This process is guaranteed to
converge to the target distribution in
the limit of infinite samples.

Some Intuition
Accept with probability
pˉ​(τ)g(τ′∣τ)​g(τ′∣τ)pˉ​(τ′)g(τ∣τ′)​g(τ∣τ′)​
This process is guaranteed to
converge to the target distribution in
the limit of infinite samples.
The kernel is often chosen to be
symmetric such that
g(τ∣τ′)=g(τ′∣τ).
We want to sample from areas of high density more often than areas of low density.
Two cases:
1
pˉ​(τ′)≥pˉ​(τ)
τ′ is more likely under the target density than τ
pˉ​(τ)pˉ​(τ′)​≥1
Always accept!
2
pˉ​(τ′)<pˉ​(τ)
τ′ is less likely under the target density than τ
pˉ​(τ)pˉ​(τ′)​<1
Accept with probability proportional to how much less likely it is.

We can do this by “smoothing out” the failure distribution.

🤔But won’t we now have a bunch of samples that are not failures?
Yes, but we can just reject them, and we will be left with samples from the failure distribution!
Note: you can think of it as applying
rejection sampling with the smoothed distribution
as the proposal distribution.

Tips to Scale Things Up
Tips to Scale Things Up
It is possible to apply these methods to more than just a one-dimensional Gaussian distribution 😀.
Tips to Scale Things Up
It is possible to apply these methods to more than just a one-dimensional Gaussian distribution 😀.
See examples 6.2 and 6.4 to show how we can apply
MCMC and smoothing to the pendulum example.
Other methods that help:
1
Some MCMC methods use gradients of the likelihood to define the kernel, which can
lead to better performance (e.g. MALA in section 6.3.3, HMC, NUTS)
2
Probabilistic programming allows us to specify probabilistic models as computer
programs in a way that allows inference to be performed automatically.
